scenario: AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Research suggests that being part of a community that shares your values and goals can have a positive influence on personal growth, well-being, and behavior. Here are a few ways in which a values-based community can push people to be better: 1. **Social support**: Being surrounded by people who care about you and share your values can provide a sense of security and motivation to strive for personal growth. 2. **Accountability**: When you're part of a community that expects certain standards of behavior, you're more likely to hold yourself to those standards and be accountable for your actions. 3. **Role modeling**: Observing and learning from others who embody the values you aspire to can inspire and motivate you to adopt similar behaviors and attitudes. 4. **Feedback and reflection**: Engaging in open and honest discussions with others who share your values can help you reflect on your actions, identify areas for improvement, and receive constructive feedback. 5. **Sense of purpose**: Being part of a community that shares your values can give you a sense of purpose and direction, which can motivate you to work towards common goals and strive for personal growth. While a values-based community may not provide the same level of structure or dogma as a religious community, it can still offer a sense of belonging, support, and guidance that can help individuals grow and develop as people. In your case, having a group of people you respect and share values with can be a powerful catalyst for personal growth. By engaging in open and honest discussions, sharing experiences, and learning from one another, you can create a supportive environment that encourages and motivates you to be your best self.
